subject: rider
name: Mounting & Dismounting
summary: Safely checking tack, mounting smoothly from a mounting block or ground, settling into the saddle, and dismounting cleanly.
purpose: Protects the horse's back and ensures the rider starts and finishes every ride safely and in control.
safety: Check girth tightness and stirrup security before mounting.
Use a mounting block whenever possible to reduce torque on the horse's back.

introductory.overview: Completing a pre-mount check, mounting smoothly without dropping onto the horse's back, and dismounting safely.

components.title: Pre-mount safety check
components.description: Checking girth, bridle/halter, and clear surroundings.

components.title: Smooth mount and dismount
components.description: Maintaining light rein contact while stepping smoothly up and settling gently, and clearing the cantle/stirrups cleanly on dismount.

introductory.learning: Mounts and dismounts a quiet horse with assistance holding the horse or adjusting tack.
introductory.proficient: Independently performs a pre-mount check, mounts smoothly using a mounting block without pulling the saddle or thumping the horse's back, and dismounts cleanly with control.

subject: rider
name: Walk
summary: Following the horse's four-beat walk in balance while maintaining calm direction, adjustable stride length, and clean halts.
purpose: Establishes independent rider balance, supple hips, quiet hands, and calm communication before faster gaits.
safety: Keep heels relaxed and hands independent of balance so you never brace on the horse's mouth.
Maintain safe spacing from other horses.

introductory.overview: Maintaining a balanced, relaxed seat at walk, asking smoothly for walk, and halting safely without bracing on the reins.

components.title: Following the four-beat motion
components.description: Allowing the pelvis to move naturally with the horse's alternating four-beat stride and keeping hands elastic so the horse's head and neck can nod freely. Common mistake: stiffening the lower back or fixing the hands, which restricts the walk and causes tension.

components.title: Basic walk starts and halts
components.description: Using light seat, leg, and voice cues to ask for walk and returning calmly to halt without pulling abruptly.

introductory.learning: Walks on a quiet horse with occasional stiffness, gripping, or reliance on the reins for balance.
introductory.proficient: Independently asks for walk, follows the four-beat motion comfortably with balanced posture and soft, non-restrictive reins (whether on light contact or a loose rein), and returns calmly to halt.

intermediate.overview: Influencing walk energy, stride length (active working walk vs. relaxed free walk), and straightness without disturbing four-beat purity.

components.title: Working walk vs. free walk
components.description: Adjusting between an active, marching working walk and a long, relaxed free walk where the horse stretches forward and down. Why it matters: preserves back suppleness and tests whether the horse stays rhythmic without constant rein hold.

components.title: Preserving pure four-beat rhythm
components.description: Common mistake: pushing too hard with the legs against tight hands, which causes the horse to hurry into a tight two-beat lateral pace (ambling/pacing) or jog. Welfare note: a restricted neck creates tension through the poll and back.

intermediate.learning: Practices adjusting walk stride length and energy with intermittent loss of four-beat rhythm or hurried steps.
intermediate.proficient: Independently rides an active, rhythmic four-beat walk, lengthens into relaxed free walk and shortens smoothly back to working walk without breaking gait or losing purity.

subject: rider
name: Trot
summary: Riding the symmetrical two-beat trot or jog in balance—progressing from balanced rising trot to diagonal control and refined, independent sitting trot.
purpose: Builds rider core stability, rhythm awareness, diagonal coordination, and supple shock absorption across a two-beat gait.
safety: Keep balance over your own base of support rather than pulling on the horse's mouth.

introductory.overview: Maintaining a balanced rising (posting) trot in rhythm with the horse, regardless of diagonal, and returning calmly to walk.

components.title: Balanced rising trot
components.description: Rising and sitting smoothly in time with the two-beat rhythm without slamming into the saddle or balancing off the reins.

introductory.learning: Rides rising trot for short stretches with occasional loss of rhythm, double-bouncing, or needing a grab strap or coaching.
introductory.proficient: Independently transitions into trot, maintains a balanced rising trot in steady two-beat rhythm for sustained stretches without pulling on the reins (regardless of diagonal), and makes a controlled transition back to walk.

intermediate.overview: Demonstrating balanced sitting and rising trot, recognizing the current posting diagonal, and deliberately changing diagonals cleanly.

components.title: Diagonal recognition and changes
components.description: Identifying the posting diagonal accurately and switching cleanly (sitting or standing two beats) when changing direction or alternating on straight lines.

components.title: Sitting trot balance
components.description: Absorbing the two-beat trot or jog motion through a supple seat without gripping, bouncing heavily, or disturbing the horse's rhythm.

intermediate.learning: Demonstrates sitting and rising trot and changes diagonals with intermittent stiffness, missed beats, or needing reminders to check the diagonal.
intermediate.proficient: Independently demonstrates both balanced sitting trot and rising trot, accurately recognizes and deliberately changes posting diagonals in both directions, and maintains steady tempo with quiet hands.

advanced.overview: Demonstrating a refined, independent sitting trot through applicable movements, transitions, and figures without interfering with the horse's back or rhythm.

components.title: Independent sitting trot in movements
components.description: Maintaining a deep, supple, independent seat and quiet hands while coordinating precise aids through turns, transitions, within-gait adjustments, and lateral work.

advanced.learning: Maintains sitting trot through basic figures but occasionally loses seat independence, hand steadiness, or rhythm during more demanding transitions or lateral movements.
advanced.proficient: Independently demonstrates a refined, supple, balanced sitting trot through applicable movements—including transitions, circles, within-gait adjustments, and lateral work—preserving horse relaxation and steady rhythm.

subject: rider
name: Canter
summary: Preparing, following, and regulating the three-beat canter or lope with balance, rhythm, clear timing, lead feel, simple lead changes, and within-gait adjustability—prioritizing horse comfort and relaxation across disciplines.
purpose: Develops hip suppleness, rhythmic core stability, accurate aid timing, and adaptable three-beat balance without equating speed or specialized maneuvers with horsemanship.
safety: Establish calm walk and trot control, clear steering, and safe spacing from other horses or hazards before cantering.
Evaluate footing, traction, slope, and turn radius before asking for canter; avoid tight turns or unbalanced departures on slick, deep, or rocky ground.
Treat repeated rushing, cross-cantering, hollowing, or one-sided lead resistance as important welfare feedback—slow down and assess saddle fit, soreness, conditioning, footing, or your own alignment.

introductory.overview: Preparing a calm depart from walk or trot, following the forward three-beat motion comfortably in a full or light/two-point seat (on light contact or a loose rein), and returning smoothly to trot or walk. Correct lead selection is not required.

components.title: Calm preparation vs. running the trot
components.description: Preparing a steady walk or balanced trot before asking lightly, rather than speeding up the trot until the horse trips or rushes into canter.

components.title: Following 3-beat feel and non-restrictive balance
components.description: Letting hips sweep cleanly with the stride in either full seat or light/two-point seat without gripping knees or balancing off the horse's mouth.

components.title: Controlled returns
components.description: Exhaling, stabilizing the core quietly, and gliding smoothly down to trot or walk while space remains clear.

introductory.learning: Departs into canter for short stretches with guidance; seat, hands, or breathing occasionally brace during transitions, or trot speeds up beforehand.
introductory.proficient: Independently prepares a balanced walk or trot, asks calmly for canter, follows the three-beat motion comfortably in full or light seat without balancing off the reins, steers simple lines/curves, and makes a controlled downward transition. Correct lead selection is not required at this level.

intermediate.overview: Preparing requested left and right leads from walk or trot, feeling which lead the horse is on without looking down, balancing curves and turns smoothly, riding calm simple lead changes, and handling wrong leads constructively.

components.title: Lead feel and anatomy without looking down
components.description: Understanding that the lead leg advances farther and feeling the corresponding forward swing of your hip/shoulder silently rather than staring down at the horse's shoulder.

components.title: Turns, generous curves, and simple lead changes
components.description: Aligning shoulders and weight smoothly around turns and generous circles or sweeping curves without leaning inward; riding calm simple lead changes through walk or trot.

components.title: Constructive adjustment and welfare
components.description: Recognizing an unintended wrong lead or disunited canter promptly, transitioning calmly back to rebalance instead of yanking, and checking comfort or rider bias if one lead is consistently difficult.

intermediate.learning: Selects leads, balances curves, and practices simple lead changes with occasional wrong-lead departs, looking down to check, leaning inward, or hurried change transitions.
intermediate.proficient: Independently prepares and asks for left and right leads from walk or trot, identifies leads by feel, maintains steady three-beat balance through turns and generous curves on light contact or a loose rein, performs clean simple lead changes, and transitions calmly to rebalance unintended or disunited leads.

advanced.overview: Refined fundamental canter mastery: regulating stride length and balance cleanly within the three-beat gait (without rushing), staying poised and aligned across varied lines, terrain, or transitions suited to the horse, and adapting thoughtfully for equine welfare. Counter-canter and flying lead changes are separate optional skills.

components.title: Within-gait adjustability (speed is not skill)
components.description: Lengthening and shortening canter stride smoothly through seat, core tone, and release timing while keeping calm three-beat rhythm rather than flattening/accelerating or pulling continuously.

components.title: Uphill balance, timing, and adaptability
components.description: Delivering subtle, clear aids tailored to stride rhythm across varied lines, curves, terrain, or transitions appropriate to the horse's build and discipline—adapting contact, posture, and pace thoughtfully.

components.title: Observing subtle fatigue or tension
components.description: Reading stiffening through the back, hurried breathing, or late hind engagement early so demands remain humane and productive.

advanced.learning: Practices within-gait lengthenings/shortenings and varied balanced canter work with intermittent flattening, bracing on the reins, crookedness, or late posture adjustments.
advanced.proficient: Independently rides a relaxed, balanced three-beat canter or lope with clear within-gait stride adjustability (lengthening and shortening without rushing), straight alignment, subtle aid timing across varied lines and transitions suited to the horse and footing, and attentive welfare-based adaptation.

subject: rider
name: Counter-Canter
summary: Intentionally riding balanced, relaxed canter or lope on the outside lead through straight lines, shallow loops, and appropriate curves without rushing or causing unintended lead swaps.
purpose: Clarifies rider seat alignment, outside-bend balance, and weight control on curved lines while serving as an optional gymnastic or discipline-specific extension of balanced canter.
safety: Build counter-canter gradually from wide shallow loops on good footing—never force tight counter-canter turns before a horse has strength and balance to carry the outside lead comfortably.
Avoid gripping or tilting to hold a lead by force; if tension builds or the horse swaps early, rebalance calmly on a straight line.

intermediate.overview: Introducing deliberate counter-canter on straight tracks and shallow curves with clear rider alignment and calm three-beat rhythm.

components.title: Understanding counter-canter alignment
components.description: Positioning subtle flexion/bend toward the leading (outside) leg while keeping rider weight centered and hips free—not leaning inward to counterbalance.

components.title: Gradual lines and release
components.description: Riding calm shallow loops off the wall/rail or slight direction changes and transitioning smoothly back to walk or trot before balance unravels.

intermediate.learning: Rides straight lines or shallow counter-canter curves with intermittent inward leaning, tension, breaking to trot, or unintended lead swaps.
intermediate.proficient: Independently prepares and maintains balanced, relaxed counter-canter along straight lines and shallow curves in both directions without rushing, tilting, or forcing the horse's neck.

advanced.overview: Sustaining poised, adjustable counter-canter through deeper curves, loops, and varied transitions while preserving rhythm, comfort, and light, adaptable aids.

components.title: Curve adaptability and timing
components.description: Matching rider weight, rib support, and light outside-lead positioning smoothly as curves deepen or straighten without disturbing three-beat balance.

components.title: Welfare and readiness awareness
components.description: Reading early hindquarter fatigue or cross-canter warning signs and adjusting bend angle, curve radius, or pace thoughtfully.

advanced.learning: Sustains deeper counter-canter loops and transitions with occasional crookedness, stiff outside shoulder, or delayed alignment adjustments.
advanced.proficient: Independently maintains poised, balanced, comfortable counter-canter through deeper loops and curves in both directions, adjusting stride and alignment fluidly on light aids without rushing or tension.

subject: rider
name: Flying Lead Changes
summary: Preparing straight, balanced canter rhythm and delivering clear, light suspension-timed aids to ask for clean flying lead changes in both directions.
purpose: Combines straightness, lead literacy, and stride-phase timing for riders choosing specialized flatwork, pattern, or jumping applications—always prioritizing horse relaxation and physical readiness.
safety: Establish calm, straight simple changes and reliable counter-canter readiness before asking for flying changes; never kick, spur harshly, or throw weight abruptly to provoke a panic swap.
Repeated late hind changes, bucking, pinned ears, or rushing often signal tension, crookedness, conditioning gaps, or back/hock discomfort—step back and evaluate comfort.

advanced.overview: Preparing straightness, balance, and quiet mental focus before asking with light, stride-timed aids for a clean, calm flying change in both directions and adapting thoughtfully to the horse's readiness.

components.title: Preparation and straightness over speed
components.description: Rebalancing the canter squarely between seat and light aids before changing leads—never speeding up or throwing torso weight violently side to side.

components.title: Timing aids to stride suspension
components.description: Delivering calm, coordinated new-lead aids clearly in the preparation/suspension window so front and hind leads change smoothly together.

components.title: Observing quality and adapting cleanly
components.description: Recognizing early anticipation, rushed changes, or late behind immediately and returning quietly to straight counter-canter, simple changes, or comfort checks as needed.

advanced.learning: Prepares and asks for flying changes with occasional rushed approaches, body twisting, unintended early swaps, late hind changes, or rider tension.
advanced.proficient: Independently prepares straight, calm, balanced canter lines, delivers clear, light, stride-timed aids for clean simultaneous flying lead changes in both directions without rushing or harshness, evaluates change quality accurately, and adapts smoothly back to simpler preparation whenever readiness or footing calls for it.

subject: rider
name: Transitions
summary: Preparing and riding smooth, balanced upward, downward, and within-gait transitions—from basic halt–walk–trot changes to accurate marks and direct transitions.
purpose: Develops rider timing, seat preparation, and responsive communication across gaits without pulling, kicking, or rushing.
safety: Prepare transitions progressively rather than abruptly hauling on the reins or kicking with conflicting leg and hand signals.

introductory.overview: Riding calm, safe progressive transitions between halt, walk, and trot with clear preparation and prompt release.

components.title: Preparing before asking
components.description: Checking posture, breathing out, and giving a light cue before escalating calmly if needed. Common mistake: pulling straight back on the reins to stop without using seat/breath, or leaning forward abruptly into trot.

components.title: Prompt release and welfare
components.description: Softening hands and legs the instant the horse responds so transitions stay calm and cooperative rather than tense or resistant.

introductory.learning: Rides halt–walk and walk–trot transitions with coaching; timing may occasionally feel abrupt, delayed, or overly rein-dependent.
introductory.proficient: Independently prepares and rides calm, progressive halt–walk–trot transitions in both directions without abrupt pulling, kicking, or losing basic balance.

intermediate.overview: Smooth progressive upward and downward transitions across halt, walk, trot, and canter—plus halting accurately on a chosen mark.

components.title: Upward and downward preparation
components.description: Using a brief rebalancing moment (half-halt) and straight alignment before asking so the horse shifts weight smoothly instead of hollowing or falling onto the forehand.

components.title: Halt on a mark
components.description: Looking ahead to plan the final strides and halt calmly and accurately at a designated cone, letter, or line without last-second pulling.

intermediate.learning: Rides progressive walk–trot–canter transitions and halts at marks with occasional rushing, lagging, or missed spots.
intermediate.proficient: Independently prepares and rides smooth, balanced progressive upward and downward transitions across halt, walk, trot, and canter, and halts calmly on a chosen mark.

advanced.overview: Balanced direct transitions (halt–trot, walk–canter, canter–walk, canter–halt) and crisp within-gait lengthenings and shortenings.

components.title: Direct transitions
components.description: Coordinating seat, core, leg, and quiet rein timing to step directly between non-adjacent gaits (such as walk–canter and canter–walk) while preserving straightness and uphill balance.

components.title: Within-gait adjustments
components.description: Lengthening and shortening stride within walk, trot, and canter without quickening into rushing or collapsing the rhythm. Common mistake: mistaking faster leg speed for genuine stride lengthening.

advanced.learning: Practices direct or within-gait transitions with intermittent loss of straightness, rhythm, or relaxation.
advanced.proficient: Independently rides balanced direct transitions and clear within-gait stride adjustments in both directions with minimal visible effort, straight alignment, and steady relaxation.

subject: rider
name: Half-Halt (Rebalancing)
summary: Using a brief, coordinated rebalancing request to gather the horse's attention and balance before a turn, figure, or transition.
purpose: Allows the rider to shift balance back from the forehand and prepare the horse smoothly without breaking gait or pulling continuously.
safety: Always release promptly after the rebalancing moment; never hold continuous backward pressure.

intermediate.overview: Coordinating seat, core, leg, and brief soft rein timing to rebalance the horse without halting—whether riding on elastic contact or a light Western rein.

components.title: Coordinated timing and release
components.description: Stabilizing the core/seat, maintaining gentle forward intention with the legs, closing the fingers briefly (or picking up light feel on a draped rein), and softening immediately as the horse rebalances.

components.title: Common mistakes and horse welfare
components.description: Common mistakes include pulling backward longer than a stride (turning a half-halt into a sustained check or tug-of-war), clamping the knees, or stalling the horse out of rhythm. Always verify the horse stays soft in the jaw and relaxed in the back.

intermediate.learning: Practices rebalancing moments with coaching; timing may occasionally stall the horse, disrupt rhythm, or turn into steady rein pull.
intermediate.proficient: Independently uses subtle, timely rebalancing requests before turns and transitions, improving the horse's posture and responsiveness without breaking rhythm or holding continuous pressure.

subject: rider
name: Steering & Navigation
summary: Guiding a horse accurately along straight lines, circles, turns, and marker patterns with appropriate bend, rhythm, and look-ahead.
purpose: Unifies arena geometry and pattern navigation into one core steering ability across walk, trot, and canter.
safety: Look ahead to plan turns early, use safe marker spacing, and keep speed within rider and footing limits.

introductory.overview: Basic steering, straight lines, recognizable ~20 m circles, turns, and simple marker patterns at walk.

components.title: Look-ahead and alignment
components.description: Looking where you intend to go and guiding shoulders and direction calmly.

components.title: Lines, circles, and simple patterns
components.description: Riding straight away from the rail, recognizable ~20 m circles, and simple cone paths at walk.

introductory.learning: Steers lines, circles, and walk patterns with occasional drifting, cutting corners, or over-reliance on one rein.
introductory.proficient: Independently steers straight lines, recognizable ~20 m circles, turns, and simple marker patterns at walk with steady rhythm and safe spacing.

intermediate.overview: Greater accuracy, rhythm, bend, and timely preparation through figures and patterns (circles, serpentines, slaloms, figure-eights) at trot.

components.title: Trot geometry and bend changes
components.description: Preparing direction and bend changes smoothly between arcs without losing rhythm or knocking markers.

intermediate.learning: Rides trot figures and patterns with late bend changes, drifting arcs, or tempo fluctuations.
intermediate.proficient: Independently rides accurate lines, circles, serpentines, and marker patterns at trot with consistent rhythm, timely preparation, and smooth changes of bend.

advanced.overview: Complex changes of direction, balance, and appropriate lead management through figures and patterns at canter.

components.title: Canter balance and lead planning
components.description: Maintaining balanced speed and choosing appropriate lead changes (simple, flying, or deliberate counter-canter) suited to the horse's training.

advanced.learning: Navigates canter patterns with intermittent loss of balance, speed control, or lead timing.
advanced.proficient: Independently rides complex canter figures and patterns with balanced speed, accurate geometry, and planned, calm lead management.

subject: rider
name: Turn on the Forehand
summary: Guiding a reasonably prepared horse to step its hindquarters laterally around a relatively steady forehand.
purpose: Develops independent hindquarter control for opening space, gate alignment, and early lateral coordination.
safety: Avoid pulling the horse backward or trapping its mouth while asking for sideways steps.

introductory.overview: From halt or very slow walk, guiding a 90–180° turn on the forehand on a cooperative horse.

components.title: Centered seat and clear request
components.description: Keeping the forehand quiet while allowing the hind legs to step across freely.

introductory.learning: Practices turns on the forehand with uneven steps, forward/backward drift, or pauses to reset.
introductory.proficient: Independently prepares the horse from halt or slow walk and guides a calm 90–180° turn on the forehand in both directions with minimal drift and soft contact.

intermediate.overview: Precise 180–360° turns on the forehand with minimal forehand pivot drift, clean rhythm, and fluid transitions in and out of walk.

components.title: Pivot steadiness and transitions
components.description: Entering from walk or halt smoothly, keeping steady four-beat stepping, and walking straight out.

intermediate.learning: Refines pivot steadiness and transitions with occasional crossing errors or loss of rhythm.
intermediate.proficient: Independently rides crisp, rhythmic turns on the forehand in both directions with steady forehand placement, no backward steps, and seamless walk transitions.

subject: rider
name: Turn on the Haunches
summary: Guiding a reasonably prepared horse from walk to step its forehand around an arc while the hindquarters remain relatively anchored.
purpose: Develops shoulder control, preparation, and balanced turning around the hindquarters.
safety: Do not force a tight pivot by pulling hard on the inside rein; prioritize steady forward walk rhythm.

introductory.overview: Guiding a calm, generous arc of the forehand around the hindquarters from walk without backing or spinning.

components.title: Walk rhythm and shoulder guidance
components.description: Keeping the horse stepping forward into a small turning arc rather than twisting or backing.

introductory.learning: Guides the forehand around the haunches with wide arcs, pauses, or occasional backward steps.
introductory.proficient: Independently guides a calm, rhythmic small-arc turn on the haunches in both directions from walk without spinning, backing, or harsh rein pull.

intermediate.overview: Compact (~1 m) rhythmic turns on the haunches with clear preparation, consistent bend, and smooth exit.

components.title: Compactness and bend
components.description: Rebalancing before the turn and maintaining four-beat walk rhythm and soft bend around a tight pivot area.

intermediate.learning: Rides tighter turns on the haunches with intermittent loss of walk rhythm or bend.
intermediate.proficient: Independently prepares and rides smooth, compact (~1 m) turns on the haunches in both directions, maintaining four-beat rhythm, relaxed bend, and clean straight exits.

subject: rider
name: Rein Back
aliases: Back through an L or corridor
summary: Guiding a reasonably prepared horse to step calmly backward in a diagonal two-beat pattern—on straight lines or through patterns like an L or corridor.
purpose: Improves responsiveness, straightness, and practical maneuvering for gates, tight spaces, and trail patterns.
safety: Never use harsh backward pulling or alternating see-saw rein pressure.
Pause and step forward to reset safely if the horse becomes tense or stuck.

intermediate.overview: Smoothly guiding 3–5 straight diagonal backward steps from a square halt, plus backing cleanly through an L or corridor.

components.title: Straight rein-back
components.description: Preparing a calm halt and inviting diagonal backward steps without rushing or raising the head.

components.title: Corridor and L-pattern application
components.description: Aligning straight and steering shoulders/hips cleanly through an L-shaped boundary without knocking rails.

intermediate.learning: Backs straight or through an L with occasional crookedness, hesitation, or boundary touches.
intermediate.proficient: Independently guides calm, straight diagonal backward steps from halt—and backs cleanly through an L or corridor without rushing, harsh rein use, or knocking boundaries—then halts or walks forward smoothly.

advanced.overview: Backing precise longer distances, serpentines, or transitions directly between rein-back and trot/canter.

components.title: Precision and direct transitions
components.description: Sustaining straightness, rhythm, and soft contact through complex backing lines and crisp forward departures.

advanced.learning: Practices extended backing patterns or direct rein-back transitions with intermittent loss of straightness or rhythm.
advanced.proficient: Independently guides accurate, relaxed rein-back lines and curves and transitions smoothly from rein-back into forward gaits without tension.

subject: rider
name: Sidepass
summary: Guiding a reasonably prepared horse to step directly sideways with even crossing of front and hind legs, in open space or over a ground rail.
purpose: Provides exact lateral positioning for gates, obstacles, and independent control of shoulders and hips.
safety: Use safe, stable ground poles on even footing when practicing over a rail.
Do not rush or force the horse sideways if it becomes confused.

intermediate.overview: Guiding calm, straight sideways steps in both directions in open space and aligned over a ground rail.

components.title: Pure sideways alignment
components.description: Balancing shoulder and hip aids so neither end lags or drifts forward/backward.

components.title: Sidepass over a rail
components.description: Aligning lengthwise over a ground pole and stepping cleanly sideways without knocking it.

intermediate.learning: Guides sideways steps with occasional forward/backward drift, lagging hips/shoulders, or touching the rail.
intermediate.proficient: Independently aligns the horse and guides several calm, straight sideways steps in both directions—including cleanly over a ground rail—without rushing or losing balance.

subject: rider
name: Leg Yield
summary: Guiding a reasonably prepared horse forward and sideways simultaneously at walk or trot with a straight body or slight flexion away from the direction of travel.
purpose: Teaches the rider to coordinate forward and lateral requests without losing rhythm, balance, or straightness.
safety: Avoid pulling backward on the reins while asking for sideways movement; ensure clear arena space.

intermediate.overview: Balanced, rhythmic leg yield in both directions at walk and trot.

components.title: Forward-lateral balance
components.description: Keeping the horse stepping forward across the diagonal without rushing, stalling, or falling through the shoulder.

intermediate.learning: Practices leg yield at walk or trot with inconsistent angle, varying rhythm, or shoulder/hip drift.
intermediate.proficient: Independently guides balanced, rhythmic leg yields in both directions at walk and trot, maintaining consistent forwardness, alignment, and smooth returns to a straight line.

subject: rider
name: Shoulder-In
summary: Guiding a horse along a straight line with the shoulders brought slightly inward and a slight, even bend away from the direction of travel.
purpose: Develops rider feel for bend, straightness, and engagement of the inside hind leg as a foundation for advanced lateral work.
safety: Build from shallow angles and short sections; never force neck bend with the reins.

intermediate.overview: Recognizable and functional shoulder-fore or shoulder-in at walk (with optional short trot experiments).

components.title: Establishing bend and line
components.description: Creating slight uniform bend before bringing the shoulders off the track and returning smoothly to straight.

intermediate.learning: Positions the shoulders in for a few walk strides with inconsistent angle, bend, or rhythm.
intermediate.proficient: Independently rides a recognizable, functional shoulder-fore or shoulder-in at walk in both directions, moving forward along the line without drifting and returning smoothly to straight. Trot proficiency is not required.

advanced.overview: Sustained shoulder-in at trot along a full long side with improved precision, consistency, balance, and coordination.

components.title: Sustained trot balance and connections
components.description: Maintaining uniform angle and bend at trot and connecting shoulder-in smoothly with figures and other movements.

advanced.learning: Sustains shoulder-in at trot with occasional loss of angle, bend, or impulsion.
advanced.proficient: Independently sustains shoulder-in at trot along a full long side in both directions with consistent angle and bend, steady rhythm and impulsion, clean entries/exits, and relaxation.

subject: rider
name: Travers (Haunches-In)
summary: Guiding a reasonably prepared horse along a straight line at walk or trot with slight inward bend (in the direction of travel), keeping the forehand on the track while carrying the hindquarters slightly inward.
purpose: Advances rider coordination, independent seat control, and feel for lateral collection.
safety: Avoid pulling the head inward or forcing the haunches over abruptly; keep segments brief and prioritize rhythm.

advanced.overview: Guiding travers in both directions at walk and trot with true inward bend, steady forehand line, and rhythmic engagement.

components.title: True inward bend
components.description: Maintaining slight bend toward the direction of travel while carrying the haunches inward (~30°) on three or four tracks.

advanced.learning: Practices travers at walk or trot with intermittent over-bending, forehand drift, or loss of rhythm.
advanced.proficient: Independently guides travers in both directions at walk and trot with true inward bend, forehand remaining on the track, hindquarters carried smoothly inward, and steady rhythm and balance.

subject: rider
name: Terrain & Obstacle Negotiation
summary: Guiding a horse safely and confidently across ground poles, bridges, tarps, water crossings, slopes, and varied terrain.
purpose: Builds balanced rider posture, clear forward support, and sound judgment across unfamiliar footing and environmental challenges.
safety: Inspect unfamiliar footing, bridges, banks, and water depth before riding across.
Never pull back on the mouth while the horse is stepping onto or balancing across an obstacle, and slow down whenever footing or visibility warrants it.

introductory.overview: Safe, controlled negotiation of straightforward obstacles and terrain (ground poles, low bridges, tarps, shallow puddles, gentle slopes) at walk.

components.title: Balanced non-interfering seat
components.description: Allowing the horse to look and place its feet while offering calm, steady forward support.

introductory.learning: Crosses straightforward obstacles or shallow water at walk with occasional hesitation, crooked lines, or tension in contact.
introductory.proficient: Independently approaches and negotiates straightforward obstacles, shallow water, and gentle terrain at walk in balance, keeping straight lines and relaxed, non-restrictive contact.

intermediate.overview: More demanding coordination across varied terrain, deeper/natural water crossings, uneven slopes, and appropriate trot work over poles or safe terrain.

components.title: Terrain balance and trot poles
components.description: Adjusting rider position (e.g., light seat/two-point) for slopes and trot poles while keeping steady rhythm.

intermediate.learning: Negotiates varied terrain or trot pole lines with intermittent loss of balance, rhythm, or line.
intermediate.proficient: Independently negotiates varied terrain, natural water crossings, and appropriate trot-level obstacle lines with balanced position, steady rhythm, and calm confidence.

advanced.overview: Complex terrain navigation and appropriate canter work (such as canter poles, open terrain lines, or combinations), with sound judgment about when to slow down.

components.title: Speed and safety judgment
components.description: Maintaining canter balance where safe and deliberately down-transitioning for bridges, deep water, slick footing, or steep drops.

advanced.learning: Practices complex terrain combinations or canter lines with occasional timing errors or late pace adjustments.
advanced.proficient: Independently navigates complex terrain and appropriate canter lines with balanced seat, accurate stride planning, and consistently sound judgment on when to slow down for safety.

subject: rider
name: Object Handling
summary: Managing gates and handling, carrying, moving, or placing objects (such as gates, bells, mail, ropes, rings, or poles) while mounted.
purpose: Integrates calm standing, one-handed control, and precise horse positioning for trail riding, ranch work, and working equitation.
safety: Keep steady control of gates so they do not swing into horse or rider; be ready to release an object and ride safely if the horse spooks.
Gates and similar fixed latch tasks are handled at halt/walk—never require unsafe gaits for an object.

introductory.overview: Fundamental object handling at halt or walk (such as picking up, carrying, or placing simple objects, ringing a bell, or basic assisted gate work).

components.title: One-handed balance at halt and walk
components.description: Reaching, holding, or placing an object smoothly without pulling on the reins or losing seat balance.

introductory.learning: Handles simple objects at halt or walk with occasional horse drift, fumbled rein transfers, or pauses.
introductory.proficient: Independently handles, carries, and places simple objects calmly at halt or walk while maintaining balanced posture and steady horse control.

intermediate.overview: Coordinated handling—such as independently opening, passing through, and closing a gate cleanly, or carrying/exchanging objects at trot where appropriate.

components.title: Gate management
components.description: Positioning beside the latch, controlling the gate through the pass-through, and latching calmly at halt/walk.

components.title: Trot object coordination
components.description: Carrying or placing appropriate objects smoothly at trot without losing rhythm or line.

intermediate.learning: Opens/closes gates or carries objects at trot with occasional repositioning, gate-swing, or tempo changes.
intermediate.proficient: Independently manages gates cleanly from halt/walk and performs coordinated object handling (including trot applications where appropriate) with calm one-handed control.

advanced.overview: Demanding handling and accurate object interaction at canter where appropriate (such as ring spearing, garrocha work, or fluid complex sequences).

components.title: Precision at speed
components.description: Maintaining straightness, rhythm, and one-handed accuracy while interacting with objects at canter where safe and appropriate.

advanced.learning: Practices demanding object interactions at canter with intermittent loss of line, balance, or accuracy.
advanced.proficient: Independently executes demanding object-handling sequences—including accurate interaction at canter where appropriate—with poised one-handed control, balanced posture, and calm horse responsiveness.
